name: MCP Manager Control

specs.name: check_backup
specs.description:
What a backup of this manager would contain — not the backup itself.

A backup is a whole server in one JSON and has no business in a chat,
so this answers with the inventory instead: how many instances, which
ones, and how many settings travel along. The file itself is downloaded
in the web UI, where the variant that includes the credentials also
lives — this tool never asks for that one.

Needs the admin password in the auth_token valve: like every route that
can hand out a credential, the manager refuses this one to a bearer
token and answers 403.

specs.name: create_tool
specs.description:
Create and install a NEW instance from raw Python code in ONE step.

Preferred over upload_tool: pass the plain Python source (no JSON
wrapping, no specs). The manager installs dependencies, validates the
code in the instance's venv, fills the Valve defaults into the editable
config and saves it. Dependencies come from the `requirements:` line in
the code's docstring, or pass them explicitly as a comma-separated
string. The new instance does NOT auto-start — call start_instance(id)
afterwards. Fails if the ID already exists (use save_tool_code to modify
an existing tool). Requires upload or full edit mode.

code.description: The complete Python source code (the full file)

id.description: Unique snake_case identifier (becomes the MCP server ID)

description.description: Short description shown in the UI and to the AI

requirements.description: Optional comma-separated pip packages (overrides the docstring)

port.description: Optional fixed port (1024-65535); omit/0 to auto-assign

specs.name: delete_content
specs.description:
Delete a stored file, or every file of one instance.

Disabled by default (allow_content_delete) and refused by the manager
as well while it runs in read-only mode. A deleted file's link stops
working immediately — that is how access to a file is withdrawn.

instance_id.description: The instance the file belongs to

filename.description: The file to delete; empty means every file of that instance

specs.name: delete_instance
specs.description:
Delete an MCP server instance and its config.

Requires upload or full edit mode. Fails with 403 while the instance is
locked in the web UI.

specs.name: export_tool
specs.description:
Export an MCP server tool as OpenWebUI-compatible JSON.

Requires full edit mode and permission to read tool source code
(allow_get_code), because the export is built from the instance's code.

instance_id.description: The instance ID (used as tool id)

name.description: Display name for the exported tool

specs.name: get_install_log
specs.description: Get the installation log for an MCP server instance.

specs.name: get_instance
specs.description: Get status and details of a specific MCP server instance.

specs.name: get_instance_config
specs.description: Get the full configuration of an MCP server instance including values.

specs.name: get_instance_specs
specs.description:
List the functions one instance provides, with parameters and usage.

Returns every function of the instance — name, description and the full
parameter schema — plus how often this instance has been used, when
last and which function that was. Read from the tool's stored specs, so
it works even while the instance is stopped.

Use this to find out what a tool can actually do before calling it, or
to check whether its descriptions are complete.

specs.name: get_runtime_log
specs.description: Get the runtime log for an MCP server instance.

specs.name: get_settings
specs.description:
How this manager is configured — everything except the secrets themselves.

Auth and edit mode, host and port, which tokens are set (never their
value), the health check and what it is allowed to restart, the file
store with its quota and retention, the update check, and the ways an
instance can be reached besides its own port: the shared port, and the
endpoints on the manager port — `/mcp/<id>` for one instance,
`/mcp/category/<name>` for a whole category. The endpoints on the
manager port are off until somebody switches them on, and the word
`category` in that path is itself a setting (category_url_segment).

Use `list_categories` for the category URLs themselves.

specs.name: get_system_stats
specs.description:
What the machine and the instances are costing right now.

Without arguments: one line for the machine — CPU, memory, disk and the
current network rate — followed by the instances that use the most
memory. With an instance id: only that instance's figures.

Memory is the instance's whole process tree, its child processes
included, so a tool that shells out is charged for what it started.
A figure shown as '?' has not been measured yet (rates and per-process
CPU need a previous sample) and is not the same as zero. If the manager
cannot measure at all, the answer says so and gives the reason — that
reason is the whole answer, do not offer another one.

top.description: How many instances to list, heaviest first (default 10)

specs.name: get_tool_code
specs.description: Get the Python source code of an MCP server tool. Requires full edit mode.

specs.name: get_tool_template
specs.description:
Returns the Python code template AND the complete JSON upload format.

Always call this before writing or uploading a new tool.
The response contains two sections:
1. The Python code template (for the 'content' field in the upload JSON)
2. The exact JSON array format that upload_tool() expects

specs.name: get_usage_stats
specs.description:
Usage statistics over all instances — what gets used, and what never.

For every known instance: calls within the given window, calls in total,
first and last use, the function used last, a per-day series, and the
same numbers broken down per function. Instances that were never used
are included with zeros — that is the point of the report.

Sorted by the calls within the window, not by the total: the total
favours whatever has been installed longest. Note that the manager
control tool and a tool router count their own traffic too, so they
rank high without being tools anyone deliberately uses.

days.description: Length of the window in days (default 7)

specs.name: list_agent_identities
specs.description:
The agents that may call this manager with a token of their own.

Id, name and role per agent, and where the identities come from. Never
a token and never a hash: a token exists once, in the second it is
issued, and this tool can neither read nor issue one — that is the web
UI's job.

The source matters. With the environment variable set, the file is
ignored entirely, which is the usual answer to "I changed the token and
nothing happened".

specs.name: list_categories
specs.description:
The category endpoints: one MCP URL per category, and what is behind it.

A category endpoint serves every *running* instance of one category as
a single MCP server, with the tools named INSTANCE.TOOL. Nothing is
configured per category — a category exists exactly as long as an
instance carries it, so this list follows the instances. The URLs below
are the truth about the path: the word after the port is a setting and
need not be "category".

Says first whether the feature is switched on at all. While it is off
the categories are still listed, but their URLs answer like any other
address this manager does not serve.

specs.name: list_content
specs.description:
List the files instances have produced, or the files of one instance.

Without an instance: one line per instance with a folder — how many
files, how much space, and how old the oldest one is. With an instance:
that folder's files with size, age and a download link.

The link is the way to hand a file to a user: it carries a token for
that one file and works in a browser without a login.

instance_id.description: Optional — the instance whose files to list

specs.name: list_instances
specs.description:
List the MCP server instances — one line each.

Status, id, category, port, how many tools the health check last saw,
and whatever is worth knowing besides: an instance that is locked, one
that requires a verified user, one that failed and why. Sixteen
instances are sixteen lines this way and several hundred without.

Ask for detail only when you actually need a field that is not in the
short form — URL, pid, version, venv or the full health record.

detail.description: True for the complete records instead of one line each

specs.name: read_content
specs.description:
Read a stored text file. Binary files are described, not dumped.

A .docx or a .png in a chat window helps nobody and costs the whole
context window — for those you get the type, the size and the download
link to hand to the user instead.

instance_id.description: The instance the file belongs to

filename.description: The file name as listed by list_content

max_chars.description: Cut the text off after this many characters (default 8000)

specs.name: reinstall_instance
specs.description:
Reinstall dependencies for an MCP server instance. Can take minutes for large packages.

Fails with 403 while the instance is locked in the web UI.

specs.name: restart_instance
specs.description:
Restart an MCP server instance.

Fails with 403 while the instance is locked in the web UI (stop and
start still work on a locked instance).

specs.name: restart_manager
specs.description: Restart the json-mcp-manager process. The manager will come back up automatically.

specs.name: save_tool_code
specs.description:
Replace the Python code of an EXISTING instance — this is the 'edit code' action.

Use this (NOT upload_tool) whenever an instance with this ID already exists,
e.g. to fix a bug, add a comment or add a method. The manager validates the
code before saving and rejects invalid code with an error list. A running
instance is then restarted automatically, and the answer says whether
that worked: saving the code and running it are two separate steps, and
a restart can fail on its own.
Requires full edit mode. Fails with 403 while the instance is locked in
the web UI — this also protects the manager control tool from editing
its own code while it is locked.

instance_id.description: The instance ID whose code to replace

code.description: The complete new Python source code (the full file, not a diff)

specs.name: start_instance
specs.description: Start an MCP server instance.

specs.name: stop_instance
specs.description: Stop a running MCP server instance.

specs.name: update_instance_category
specs.description:
Set, change or clear the manager category of an existing instance.

Category is display/filter metadata in the MCP manager. It does not
modify the tool JSON or Python code and does not require a restart.
Pass an empty string to remove the category. Requires upload or full
edit mode and fails with 403 while the instance is locked in the web UI.

category.description: New category, or an empty string to clear it

specs.name: update_instance_dependencies
specs.description:
Replace the pip dependencies of an existing instance and reinstall them.

Sets install.dependencies to the given list. The manager prepares the
instance venv as part of the update and restarts a running instance when
required; no second reinstall request is sent. Requires upload or full
edit mode and fails with 403 while the instance is locked in the web UI.

dependencies.description: Full list of pip package specs (replaces the old list)

specs.name: update_instance_lifecycle
specs.description:
Switch an instance's auto-start and restart-on-change on or off.

auto_start — start this instance automatically when the manager starts.
restart_on_change — restart it by itself after its configuration changed.

These two are **not** Valve values. Do not try to set them through
update_instance_values: that call takes only the tool's own valves and
refuses a name that is not one.

Pass "true" or "false" for the setting you want to change and leave the
other empty — an empty argument means "leave it as it is".

specs.name: update_instance_values
specs.description:
Set/merge Valve values (configuration) of an existing instance.

Merges the given keys into the instance's editable config values, e.g.
an API key or a base URL. Other values are kept (send only the keys you
want to change). Requires upload or full edit mode and fails with 403
while the instance is locked in the web UI.

Only the tool's **own valves** are accepted here; a name that is not one
is refused, and the refusal lists the valves this instance has. In
particular auto_start and restart_on_change are not valves — they are
set with update_instance_lifecycle.

The manager normally restarts a running instance automatically when
restart_on_change is enabled. The response states whether that restart
happened. Only ask about a manual restart when the manager did not
restart an instance that is currently running.

values.description: Mapping of valve name to value (only the keys to change)

specs.name: update_instance_venv
specs.description:
Move an instance to a different virtual environment (venv).

Sets the instance's venv, (re)installs its dependencies there and — if the
instance is running — restarts it so the change applies immediately. The
target venv is created automatically if it does not exist yet. Requires
upload or full edit mode and fails with 403 while the instance is locked
in the web UI.

venv.description: Target venv name (created on demand; letters, digits, _ and -)

specs.name: upload_tool
specs.description:
Create and install a NEW tool instance from a JSON definition.

Only for NEW tools: fails if the ID already exists — in that case use
save_tool_code(instance_id, code) to change the existing tool instead.
The manager validates the Python code on upload and rejects invalid code
with an error list. Requires upload or full edit mode.

Workflow for a new tool:
1. get_tool_template() — get the exact JSON format and code template
2. validate_tool_code(code) — repeat until there are no errors
3. upload_tool(json_content, category) — JSON must be an array; category is
   stored separately as manager metadata and never inserted into the JSON
4. start_instance(id) — uploaded instances do not start automatically

json_content.description: JSON array string — call get_tool_template() to see the format

category.description: Optional manager category (for example "Smart Home"); not written into the JSON

specs.name: validate_tool_code
specs.description:
Validate Python tool code: syntax check, runtime inspection and schema generation.

ALWAYS call this before upload_tool or save_tool_code and fix every reported
error first — the manager rejects invalid code anyway, so validating early
saves a round trip. Returns valid, errors, warnings, the generated tool
specs and the Valves defaults. Requires full edit mode.

code.description: The Python source code to validate

instance_id.description: Optional — validate in this instance's venv so its installed third-party dependencies resolve (recommended when editing an existing instance; older managers ignore this parameter)

meta.description: Manage json-mcp-manager via MCP — list, start, stop, restart instances, view logs, upload tools, edit code and more. Security levels are enforced server-side.
